question: In previously untreated EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC, does osimertinib improve outcomes compared with standard EGFR-TKIs?
claim: In previously untreated EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC, osimertinib significantly improved progression-free survival compared with standard EGFR-TKIs (gefitinib or erlotinib).
source_title: Osimertinib in Untreated EGFR-Mutated Advanced Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer
quoted_or_source_note: Abstract: median PFS 18.9 months with osimertinib vs 10.2 months with standard EGFR-TKIs; HR 0.46 (95% CI 0.37-0.57), P<0.001; N=556 randomized 1:1.
agent_summary: FLAURA trial directly supports a treatment-efficacy claim for osimertinib over standard EGFR-TKIs in first-line EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC.

question: In previously untreated advanced ALK-positive nonsquamous NSCLC, does crizotinib improve outcomes compared with pemetrexed-plus-platinum chemotherapy?
claim: In previously untreated advanced ALK-positive nonsquamous NSCLC, crizotinib significantly improved progression-free survival compared with pemetrexed-plus-platinum chemotherapy.
source_title: First-line crizotinib versus chemotherapy in ALK-positive lung cancer
quoted_or_source_note: Abstract: median PFS 10.9 months with crizotinib vs 7.0 months with chemotherapy; HR 0.45 (95% CI 0.35-0.60), P<0.001; N=343.
agent_summary: PROFILE 1014 directly supports a treatment-efficacy claim for crizotinib over pemetrexed-plus-platinum chemotherapy in first-line ALK-positive advanced NSCLC.

question: In advanced nonsquamous NSCLC (adenocarcinoma), does cisplatin plus pemetrexed improve overall survival compared with cisplatin plus gemcitabine?
claim: In the adenocarcinoma histology subgroup of advanced NSCLC, cisplatin plus pemetrexed showed statistically superior overall survival compared with cisplatin plus gemcitabine.
source_title: Phase III study comparing cisplatin plus gemcitabine with cisplatin plus pemetrexed in chemotherapy-naive patients with advanced-stage non-small-cell lung cancer
quoted_or_source_note: Abstract: adenocarcinoma subgroup n=847, median OS 12.6 months (cisplatin/pemetrexed) vs 10.9 months (cisplatin/gemcitabine); overall trial N=1725 met its noninferiority endpoint.
agent_summary: This trial supports a narrow histology-specific efficacy claim for pemetrexed-plus-platinum chemotherapy in adenocarcinoma; the overall-population result was noninferiority, not superiority, so the claim is scoped to the adenocarcinoma subgroup only.

question: What recurrent molecular alterations does comprehensive genomic profiling identify in resected lung adenocarcinoma?
claim: Molecular profiling of resected lung adenocarcinoma identifies recurrent driver-associated alterations in EGFR, MET, ERBB2, and RIT1, but this profiling study alone does not establish drug efficacy for any of these targets.
source_title: Comprehensive molecular profiling of lung adenocarcinoma
quoted_or_source_note: Abstract: molecular profiling of 230 resected lung adenocarcinomas; aberrations in NF1, MET, ERBB2 and RIT1 occurred in 13% of cases; EGFR mutations were more frequent in female patients.
agent_summary: TCGA row establishes molecular context only; must not be converted into a treatment-efficacy claim for any of the listed genes.

question: In EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC treated with osimertinib, is a co-occurring TP53 mutation associated with worse progression-free survival?
claim: In a retrospective cohort of EGFR-mutated NSCLC patients treated with osimertinib, co-occurring TP53 mutation was associated with significantly shorter progression-free survival than EGFR mutation alone; this is a prognostic/biomarker association within a single-arm cohort, not a randomized drug-efficacy comparison.
source_title: New therapeutic approaches for EGFR mutated non-small cell lung cancer on osimertinib era
quoted_or_source_note: Abstract: 58 stage IV EGFRmut NSCLC patients on osimertinib; TP53 was the most frequent co-mutation (70% of the 44.1% with a second co-mutation); TP53 co-mutation HR for PFS 21.6 (95% CI 2.77-169), P<0.001; OS trend HR 3.10 (95% CI 0.89-10.8), P=0.062, not statistically significant.
agent_summary: This row is literature-backed for a prognostic association but is deliberately kept as molecular_context, not literature_evidence for drug efficacy, because the study is a single-arm retrospective cohort, not a comparative efficacy trial.

question: Does TP53 co-mutation status also predict reduced response to ALK inhibitors in ALK-positive NSCLC?
claim: TP53 co-mutation is expected to confer reduced treatment response to ALK inhibitors as well as EGFR-TKIs in NSCLC, by analogy to the EGFR-TKI/TP53 finding.
quoted_or_source_note: No PMID or DOI was found for a TP53-ALK-inhibitor claim during this search; the statement extrapolates from the EGFR/TP53 finding above (PMID 40414016) to a different gene-drug context.
agent_summary: This is a plausible biological extrapolation, not a verified claim. It must not be reported as literature evidence until a supporting ALK-specific source is found and checked.
